messages.content: Get the protein sequence of human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin, and rat hemoglobin and their 3D models

function.name: protein_info_get_sequence_and_3D
function.description: Retrive the sequence and 3D models of proteins. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

model_3d.description: Set true to get 3D model of the protein.

We have three proteins: human HbA1c (which is glycated hemoglobin A1c), normal hemoglobin (likely human hemoglobin A), and rat hemoglobin. We need to provide the protein names. For human HbA1c, we might use "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" or "Hemoglobin subunit beta"? But HbA1c refers to glycated hemoglobin A1c, which is the glycated form of hemoglobin A. The sequence is same as normal hemoglobin but with glycation at N-terminal valine of beta chain? Actually HbA1c is formed by non-enzymatic glycation of the N-terminal valine of the beta chain. So the sequence is same as normal hemoglobin A. But we can still request the sequence. For normal hemoglobin, we can request "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" and "Hemoglobin subunit beta". But maybe they want the entire hemoglobin? We can request "Hemoglobin A" or "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" and "beta". For rat hemoglobin, we can request "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" and "beta" from rat.

But the function expects a single protein name. We can call it multiple times. Let's call for "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" and "Hemoglobin subunit beta" for human, and "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" and "Hemoglobin subunit beta" for rat. For HbA1c, maybe "Hemoglobin subunit beta" with glycation? But we can just request "Hemoglobin subunit beta" for human. But the user specifically wants "human HbA1c, normal hemoglobin, and rat hemoglobin". So we can interpret "normal hemoglobin" as human hemoglobin A (both alpha and beta). And "rat hemoglobin" as rat hemoglobin A (alpha and beta). And "human HbA1c" as the glycated form of human hemoglobin A beta chain. But the function may not support glycation. We can just request the sequence of the beta chain. But we can mention that glycation occurs at N-terminal valine.

Thus we will call the function for each protein: "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" (human), "Hemoglobin subunit beta" (human), "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" (rat), "Hemoglobin subunit beta" (rat). For HbA1c, we can request "Hemoglobin subunit beta" (human) and note glycation. But maybe we can request "Hemoglobin subunit beta" with glycation? Not possible. So we will just provide the sequence and 3D model of the beta chain.

Alternatively, we could request "Hemoglobin A" as a whole. But the function likely expects a UniProt ID or name. We can use "Hemoglobin subunit alpha" (UniProt P69905 for human alpha, P68871 for human beta). For rat, alpha: P02352, beta: P02353. For HbA1c, we can use "Hemoglobin subunit beta" (P68871). We'll provide the sequence and 3D model.

Let's call the function four times.
